name: A Belated ‘Sacrifice’ — Part One

date.source: The thread's own posting date on the fed's own board.

notes: The first half of one broadcast from The Pyramid in Memphis, posted overnight on 17 August 2005; the second half went up the following night as its own thread and carries Matches Two to Four and Segments Five to Nine. Angelo Marcello's first match in the promotion, and Trent Hawk arriving by white limo with the UCW championship under his coat — which Headmaster Al confiscated at the door.

appearances.note: Opened the show telling the Sonic Death Monkeys to be out of the building, was seized by both Acolytes over it, and later confiscated Trent Hawk's UCW championship at the door.
Thanked the Headmaster for the night off, seconds before the Acolytes came down the hall.
At ringside for J.P. Ruthless, and levelled with a foreign object before the bell.
At ringside for J.P. Ruthless, and levelled with a foreign object before the bell.
Grabbed the Headmaster by the shirt, called him “Headmaster Chimp”, and powerbombed the already-beaten J.P. Ruthless after the match.
Told Bradshaw to put the Headmaster down and then seized him himself.
At ringside for his son's debut.
At ringside for his cousin's debut, and shook his head the moment Angelo's back was turned.
At ringside for his nephew's debut.

Arrived by white limo in a white fur coat with the UCW championship under it, and was made to leave the belt outside — “This isn't the UCW. This is the Foundation of Brutality. No UCW titles allowed.”

matches.note: Angelo Marcello's debut. His uncle and his cousin levelled Drowneb and Skitz with a foreign object at ringside first; Marcello opened Ruthless up, delivered four consecutive powerbombs and covered him. After the bell Bradshaw powerbombed Ruthless again — “Poor, J.P.. That's two for him in one night!”

name: A belated ‘Sacrifice,’ part deux

date.source: The thread's own posting date on the fed's own board.

notes: The second half of the same Memphis broadcast, posted the following night; the fed's own match and segment numbering runs straight on from Part One. Three matches, all with declared finishes — a clean pin, a disqualification and a tag title-less main event — and a black limo whose passenger never appears. The booker's own reply closes it: “Another great show, Laces. Congrats to all the winners. Keep up the RPing, guys.”

appearances.note: Interfered in Match Three, pedigreed Chris Workman, and then talked Headmaster Al into rehiring him on the spot.
Rehired Triple H, and announced a tournament to crown a new F.O.B. “JOB-IS-NOW-ON-THE-LINE” champion.
Named in full on this show, watching a black limo pull up outside The Pyramid that nobody ever got out of.

matches.note: Hawk attacked from behind before the bell and put Jacobs through the steel steps; Jacobs missed one cover, ducked the superkick, and hit Out of the Dark for the three. “Trent Hawk of the defunct UCW, has been upset here!” Hawk then superkicked the referee. This is the FoB match the UCW holding's own record knew about and could not place.

WINNER-FLIP: the card bills Sweeten first and Workman won. Workman had Sweeten covered after a superkick when Triple H slid in, broke it up and pedigreed him; the referee called for the bell. “The winner of this match by a disqualification... CHRIS WORKMAN!”

WINNER-FLIP: the card bills The Acolytes first and The Butlers won. Jeffery came in behind the referee's back for the Clean Up and Desmond hooked the leg; Bradshaw was still climbing through the ropes at three. Billed the Acolytes' qualifying match — the Sonic Death Monkeys were not in the building and they lost anyway.

name: FoB: Rebirth — Hour 1

date.source: The show's own header, “September 20th, 2005 From Austin, Texas”.

notes: The fed's own September supercard, from Austin, Texas, opening on a seven-man over-the-top battle royal won by Mr. Australia and a number one contender's tag match that finished backstage. The commentary promises SEVEN matches; five hours were posted to the fed's own results forum and the archive holds the first and the third. Hours 2, 4 and 5 were never captured — hour 4 and hour 5 include the four-team tag title tournament final The Butlers won and the thirty-one man Rebirth match Christopher Daniels won. A video package inside this hour replays John Lennex's own scaffolding-match title defence against Mr. One Night Stand from the belt's first life; that is archival footage and earns no row of its own here.

appearances.note: Called the battle royal, and recalled that SBM had won the previous year's Rookie Invitational.
Backstage with Al Snow to introduce the night's video packages, listing the FoB Championship's holders — “Chaos, Crockett, Lennex, Nob…”
Announced that the promotion would crown both new tag team champions and a new FoB Champion that night.

matches.stipulation: The 2nd Annual Rookie Invitational Battle Royal — over the top rope, pinfall or submission

eliminations.note: Forced over the top by the pair working together.
Clotheslined over the top the instant after Mitchell had raised Carlito's arm.
The show bills him Mark Garrett on the card and Matt Garrett twice in the body.
Pressed overhead and thrown onto the guard rail.
Novak charged at Mr. Australia, who dived out of the way, and collided with Carlito on the apron.

matches.note: WINNER-FLIP: the card lists the winner last. Seven men; six eliminations; “Here is your winner…MR. AUSTRALIA!!!!”

matches.stipulation: Number one contender's match for the FoB Tag Team Championships
matches.note: Finished in the backstage area beside a dumpster: Mouse dropped Punk face-first off a trash can and both men lay unconscious while the referee counted, T-Bone stopping Cabana with a double axe handle a half-second before three. The Detroit Street Thugs' own roleplay names the losing team Future Perfect.

name: FoB: Rebirth — Hour 3
notes: The third hour opens on the crowd still reacting to the tag title tournament final that ran in an hour the archive never captured, and holds one match: the first of the night's two main events. It closes on a long video package replaying the Foundation of Brutality's own 2004 Rebirth World Title match — Chaos defending against Carnage and Robbie Crockett, and losing it after Mortis ran in and hit him with Hell Bent — announced by Michael Buffer. That is archival footage of a show the archive never captured and earns no match row here; it is registered instead as fob-rebirth-2004. The fed's own Championship Lineage records that Christopher Daniels beat thirty other men in the reinstated-title Rebirth match later this night; that hour was never captured either.

matches.stipulation: Triple threat grudge match — the first of two main events
matches.note: The Body Breaker jumped Daniels on the entrance ramp before his music played and DDT'd him on the steel; Morley hit a suicide dive, a Reality Shot for a two count and two Blue Thunder Bombs before being dropkicked off the top rope onto the ramp. Daniels finished with the Best Moonsault Ever. The commentary spends the match wondering whether winning it costs him the Rebirth match later the same night; it did not.

name: F.O.B. Sacrifice
notes: Held only as its own narrative recap thread, posted 8 October 2005 — a dark match and five matches summarised with their finishes, two of them ruled for neither team. The show script itself was never captured, and the recap's own author signed off “That's it. I'm dead. GOODNIGHT, EVERYBODY!” The Marcello interrogation runs through all six segments and closes the show.

appearances.note: Billed “Coach” CM Punk at ringside for Kid Kash and Frankie Kazarian, and half the reason the match was thrown out.
Ran down to the ring during the brawl that ended Match One.
At ringside with the New Age Outlaws, getting in their way, and fighting Chyna on the floor as the fall was scored.
At ringside with the New Age Outlaws; the ringside fight between her and X-Pac decided the match.

Pulled all four Marcellos into his office one at a time over the kidnapping of Desmond Butler and the beating of his brother, threatened to fire and have arrested whoever did it, and got his answer from the youngest of them.
Questioned first, and denied it coyly.
Questioned second, and denied all knowledge.
Tried to sit in on his son's interrogation as a translator and was made to leave.

Questioned last, told the Headmaster “Nothing”, and then told his family exactly what he had not said — including that it was Trinity who had put the hit out on The Butlers. The Headmaster was standing in the doorway.
Called Trey Deep's farewell “one, last ‘Trey Deep original’”.
Named as having been kidnapped, and the reason for the interrogations; he is not on the card.
Named as having been beaten in the same attack; he is not on the card.

matches.note: “Before Sacrifice went on the air, Drowneb and Novak battled to a no-contest, when the fight took to the outside of the ring, where both men were counted out.”

Odes claimed stomach cramps before the bell and Drowneb wrestled in his place — his second match inside twenty minutes — while Odes interfered from the floor anyway. CM Punk seconded Kash and Kazarian; Colt Cabana ran in; it became a four-on-three brawl and the referee threw it out. “Winners: Neither team.”
The veterans had the newcomers beaten until X-Pac and Chyna started fighting outside the ring; Road Dogg was rolled up mouthing “Oh, man. Not again.” “Winners: The Immortal Outlaws.”

WINNER-FLIP: the card bills Trey Deep and Randy Orton first and the Detroit Street Thugs won. Orton refused to help his partner and then Trey Deep — “the Artist Formerly Known as ‘Carnage’”, already promoted to Underground — walked out on him in return; Mouse took the fall with the Shooting Star Press. “Winners: The Number-one contenders, The Detroit Street Thugz.”

Mr. Australia spent the match in a trance on the top rope refusing tags; Bourne finished a two-on-one Body Breaker with Marshall Law. “Winners: Bourne and Kronik.” Body Breaker powerbombed his own partner afterwards.

The recap ends the sentence on the finish — “Daniels scored the last run, nailing Garrett with the Angel's Wings,” — without a winner line. The following week's own show declares it: “We see a clip of Christopher Daniels beating Mark Garrett in a rematch last week at Sacrifice to retain his FoB Heavyweight Championship” (the fed's own FoB Sacrifice, “A New Chapter”, 13 October 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/fob-sacrifice-2005-10-13.html)). The recap also records that Garrett had beaten Daniels the week before — “the upset from last week”, “his opponent, whom he'd beaten only a week earlier” — on a show whose own thread was never captured.

name: FoB Sacrifice: A New Chapter

date.source: The show's own header, “October 13th, 2005: ‘A New Chapter’”.

notes: The fed's debut in The Igloo, nine matches long — the most matches on any surviving FoB card — and the show on which Al Snow left, Sean O'Haire abolished the office of general manager, and the written rules for the reinstated Wrath Division were read out on camera off a yellow sheet of paper dated 10 October 2005. Two of the nine were interrupted and never ruled on. The booker's own reply thanks “the viewers for the most viewed FoB show since May 16, 2004.”

appearances.note: Introduced Al Snow's farewell and then abolished the office — “That's right. Who needs a General Manager?”
Said goodbye in verse and left; his memo reinstating the Wrath Division, dated 10 October 2005 and signed Allan Snow, was read out on camera off a yellow sheet of paper later in the show.
Led Blood's pre-match talk in their own locker room — “Or they'll end up cova'd in BLOOD.”
In the Blood locker room, glad not to have drawn his own stablemates.
In the Blood locker room.

Aired a promotional video for Baxter Baxter before his match and then held a mock psychiatrist's session with him afterwards, prescribing him “a healthy prescription of Bubba Ray Dudley” and the Wrath Division.
Named by Dr. Greenwood as Baxter Baxter's opponent for the following week.
Led Balthamel to the ring in robes and a cowl and called the FoB Heavyweight Championship, and its holder, nothing.
Debuted with Fight Against Prejudice immediately after the tag title change and put T-Bone in the Camel Clutch.
Hit Mouse and then T-Bone with the Hindusault.
Walked his two clients down and nodded when it was finished.

matches.note: No finish and no ruling: both men were worn out and rising when a countdown appeared on the screen, and Chris Jericho ran in and put both of them out of the ring. The fed never declared a result.
Orton went for the RKO repeatedly and was pushed off every time; a Lionsault for two, then an enzuigiri into the Walls of Jericho, “which resulted in the tapping of Randy Orton.”

WINNER-FLIP: the card bills the winners last. CounterStrike mauled Degeneration X and were thrown out for not returning to their corner, Kronik taking the microphone to quit the promotion on the way up the ramp; Tru-Cap hit the Silver Bullet and Big Buck finished Billy Gunn with a Jackknife Powerbomb. Blood's first FoB win.

Baxter could not get his bear hug on until a clothesline turned him red and the crowd started chanting; he applied it to a man draped on the second rope and then DDT'd him off it for the three. Dynasty left on a stretcher.
Carlito spat apple in Mr. Australia's eyes, blinded him, and finished with the modified neckbreaker. “Carlito's Way! This match is over! The cool one prevails!”

No finish and no ruling: Robinson had Avenger beaten and was on the top rope for the One Hour Photo when Balthamel's entrance began; Robinson climbed down and left the arena, and Balthamel chokeslammed and Tarmon Gai'don'd the man Robinson had left behind.

WINNER-FLIP: the card bills Balthamel first and David Jax won. Moriden pushed Jax off the top rope, then took the Balefire himself when Jax reversed the whip; Jax rolled Balthamel into a small package with a handful of rope. “Both men resorted to dirty deeds. But Jax was able to execute them in a better fashion.”

WINNER-FLIP: the card bills the champions first and the challengers won. Desmond was never able to tag out — at one point Mouse put a mousetrap in front of him — and took the Mouse Trap and then Detroit Rock City. The title change the fed's own lineage dates to 13 October 2005.
Daniels's second title defence in two weeks. Hardy's nose was broken by the STO and bled the rest of the match; Daniels finished with the Angel's Wings and Hardy did not move for the count.

name: FoB Sacrifice: A Cannon's Past — Exposed

date.source: The thread's own posting date on the fed's own board.

notes: Five matches and three of the fed's own set pieces: a full Eddy Guerrero tribute video opening the show, five instalments of a video series called A Haunting Past narrating Matt Stanton's whole PWE career backwards through TPG, Revenge, Underground and Carnage footage, and the white paper being stolen out of Chris Jericho's hands in a blackout. Eight matches, every one with a declared outcome — including a double count-out the ring announcer gave to nobody. The last FoB card the archive holds.

appearances.note: Opened the broadcast proper — “Eduardo Gory Guerrero, we'll miss you.”
Rode down the entrance ramp in Blood's car and stood in the ring while Gangsta Thunda demanded the tag titles at Decimation.
Rode down the entrance ramp in Blood's car.
Appeared on the tron to tell Evolution, Blood and The Fear that a tag team of her own was coming — “A position of great distinction or superiority.”
Hosted the fourth edition of Dr. Greenwood's Diagnosis in a ring dressed as a psychiatrist's office, was interrupted five times, and sent everyone who interrupted him to the Wrath Division.
Led the New Breed into Greenwood's segment and introduced all three of them.
Introduced by Katrina as the New Breed's technician.
Introduced by Katrina.
Introduced by Katrina.
Walked into Greenwood's segment, did the thigh feel and the bite, and never spoke.
Interrupted Greenwood and was interrupted himself four words in.
Arrived with his father and was cut off mid-introduction.
Brought to the ring by his son and named “my father, Ocsar”.
One of the three who came out last, demanding insight.
Ambushed Matt Stanton after the main event, beat him bloody and had him up for the F-5 before AJ Styles broke it up.
Returned to break up Alex Hoffman's attack and helped Matt Stanton up the ramp — “So I called up an old friend.”
Named by Christopher Daniels in his own pre-match promo among the men he had beaten.

matches.note: “Your winners @ 5:32 via pinfall and Detroit Rock City…The Detroit Street Thugs!” The challengers are billed Darkness Reigns in the match header and Odd Destruction in the body of the same match.

matches.stipulation: Handicap match — The Fear v. The Aussie Connection & Size Does Matter
matches.note: Two against four. The card names two opposing teams and four opposing wrestlers and never says which two men are in which team, so the opposition is filed as one side. Odes finished Blitz with Shiva's Wrath. “Your winners @ 6:49 via Shiva's Wrath and submission, The Fear!”

Carlito arrived stumbling, fell over before Flair could reach him, and then dropped a set of steel steps on himself; both men were counted out. “Your winner….nobody…” The dizzy spells are the reason he leaves in an ambulance, and the reason Chris Jericho has to read out the white paper alone.

Todd answered a lock-up offer with a high five and then a shoulder to the stomach, and had to be talked into the half Boston crab by Chris Jericho at ringside. “Your winner @ 5:21 via Half Boston Crab and submission…TODD.”
Jericho took the legs away and finished with the Walls of Jericho. “Your winner @ 7:31 via Walls of Jericho and submission…Chris…Jericho!!!” — his third straight submission win.
Bingham dominated the first half and then kicked Baxter in the face; Baxter went red and did not stop punching. “Your winner @ 8:31 via Paranoia and pinfall…Baxter...Baxter!”

matches.stipulation: For a shot at the Wrath Championship at Decimation
matches.note: A thumb to the eye, a DDT, a scoop slam and the Lightin' Bullet. “Your winner @ 8:34 via Lightin' Bullet and pinfall…GANGSTA…THUNDA!” The winner earned a match with Baxter Baxter the following week, whose winner would then pick his own Decimation opponent for the reinstated Wrath Championship.

Stanton dropped his microphone mid-promo and jumped the champion; eighteen and a half minutes later Daniels reversed the Heavy Artillery and hit the Angel's Wings. “Your winner @ 18:39 via Angel's Wings and pinfall….THE FALLEN ANGEL…CHRISTOPHER…DANIELS!!!”

name: FoB Decimation

date.source: Derived from three of the fed's own documents that agree: the 19 November show booked the reinstated Wrath Championship match and the triple threat TLC tag title match for Decimation; the fed's own roleplay forum carries both of those matches with their threads closing 7 December; and the fed's own Championship Lineage dates both resulting title changes — Baxter Baxter over Gene Snitsky for the Wrath Title, and The Fear over the Detroit Street Thugs for the tag titles — to 8 December 2005.

evidence.source: the fed's own FOB PRESENTS results forum as the board rendered it on 15 December 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/forum-fob-presents-135.html)

evidence.source: the fed's own published Championship Lineage, kept as a running board post (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/fob-supercard-schedule-2005-09-29.html)
evidence.note: Two title changes dated 8 December 2005 — the reinstated FoB Wrath Championship to Baxter Baxter over Gene Snitsky, and the FoB Tag Team Championships to The Fear over the Detroit Street Thugs — matching two of the matches this card was built around.

evidence.source: the fed's own FoB Sacrifice, “A Cannon's Past: Exposed”, 19 November 2005 (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/fob-sacrifice-2005-11-19.html)
evidence.note: Booked on the 19 November show: the TLC triple threat for the tag titles, and the reinstated Wrath Championship match whose participants two more matches were still deciding.

evidence.source: the fed's own Supercard Schedule, which fixes Decimation to November (/promotions/pwe-inc/archive/fob-supercard-schedule-2005-09-29.html)
evidence.note: The calendar says November and the card ran on 8 December; the disagreement is the promotion's own and is recorded rather than resolved.

notes: The Foundation of Brutality's own November supercard, run in December. Its results thread was never captured, but the fed's own lineage dates two title changes to the night — the reinstated Wrath Championship, decided by the division whose rules had been read off a yellow sheet of paper eight weeks earlier, and the tag titles. The fed's own roleplay forum carries nine of its matches, including five rounds of an Eddy Guerrero Memorial Cup and a six-man tag whose stipulation was the right to a piece of paper.

name: FoB: Rebirth (2004)

notes: THE CARD THAT MAY NEVER HAVE HAPPENED. Thirteen matches were booked on the fed's own roleplay forum in the week after Decimation — an Eddy Guerrero Memorial Cup round, two Wrath Championship matches, a tag title defence, the Hoffman–Stanton grudge match the November main event had set up — and no results thread for any of them exists in the fed's own results forum. Some or all of them may have been intended for the Genesis supercard the fed still had carded for January 2006; the record does not say. Held as one row rather than none, on the billed-appearance doctrine: the museum can hold a promise without claiming it was kept.
